name: Lansoprazole
summary: Pharmacologically a close cousin of omeprazole, but its orally-disintegrating and NG-tube-compatible formulations are the real differentiator.
good: Patients with dysphagia, NG/PEG tube feeding, or pediatric dosing — the granules disperse in water or juice and remain effective.
bad: No specific advantage over omeprazole if the patient can swallow a standard capsule.
clinicalPearls: The orally-disintegrating tablet and sprinkle-capsule formats make this the practical default whenever a patient cannot swallow a normal capsule.
pharmacodynamics: Comparable to omeprazole at equivalent doses.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Days to full steady-state effect, as with other classic PPIs.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: CYP2C19-dependent, similar variability profile to omeprazole.

indications: GERD, ulcer disease, H. pylori eradication; pediatric and enteral-feeding-friendly formulations widely available.
interactionNotes: Same CYP2C19-mediated class cautions (clopidogrel, azole antifungals, atazanavir, iron).
